## Accessibility and installation corrections

The missed-work audit authorized a small, separate accessibility layer. Original Bootstrap CSS interfaces and JavaScript bundles remain available. The documentation and local examples load the separate TQ layer after Bootstrap and before initializing enhanced components. It manages tooltip hover/focus/Escape, paused carousel startup and explicit Play/Pause, and persistent form errors with field associations and an error summary. See [integration instructions](../docs/INTEGRATION.md) for loading order, module APIs, disposal and author responsibilities.

Both dashboard examples provide a named chart, description and keyboard-operable native data disclosure containing the exact seven plotted values. The theme control occupies its own normal-flow row only on the bottom-navbar and navbar comparison examples, resolving the measured control collision. Scrollable code blocks receive named keyboard regions only while their actual content overflows; the observer reassesses viewport/font/text-size changes. Ordinary bright links/outline controls use explicit native contrasting surfaces, and list metadata retains readable opacity. Numeric-opacity teaching fixtures preserve their true utility values and have visible diagnostic explanations and equivalent readable labels; they are not certified reading-text combinations.

The homepage and download documentation point to the actual local TQ downloads and CSS integration. Public package-manager commands and external hosted starters are explicitly labelled as upstream Bootstrap, with stock colours. No TQ package has been published to npm or an external starter service. Native hosted search, external imagery, outbound links and hosted starters may need a network connection. This is not a claim of universal WCAG conformance.

The original Bootstrap distributions remain intact. A separate optional enhancement runtime is supplied for the accessibility defaults used by the local docs/examples. Load it after Bootstrap and before any tooltip/carousel/custom-validation initializer:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="dist/css/bootstrap.min.css">
<script src="dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"></script>
<script src="dist/tq/tq-accessibility.min.js"></script>
<script>TQAccessibility.init();</script>
```

Initialise enhanced tooltips with `TQAccessibility.createTooltip(element, nativeOptions)` instead of first creating a separate native tooltip instance. Use tooltips only for short non-interactive text; put actionable help in a named dialog. Enhanced carousels start paused, supply Play/Pause controls and respect reduced motion and focus. Enhanced `form.needs-validation` workflows provide persistent feedback associations and an error summary; remove any duplicate upstream demonstration submit handler. Keep actual labels, constraints and useful error text in the markup.

The ESM build is `dist/tq/tq-accessibility.esm.js`, exporting `init`, `createTooltip`, `enhanceCarousel`, `enhanceValidation` and `dispose`. Pass the imported Bootstrap namespace through the `bootstrap` option when not using the global bundle. The layer preserves native component instances, methods, events and data attributes. Use the layer’s disposal function when removing an enhanced region; then dispose any other native instances you created. Retest your own initialization and dynamic-content workflow.

## TQ downloads and upstream packages

Use the local compiled download for TQ colours. Copy its `dist` directory to your own site and include exactly one TQ Bootstrap CSS file. The source download contains the TQ Sass inputs and reproducible build instructions. Public `npm install bootstrap`, yarn, RubyGems, Composer and CDN packages install stock Bootstrap; they do not contain this independently packaged theme. Keep their original JavaScript imports if needed, and replace their default stylesheet with the local TQ CSS. Do not load both copies of the CSS.

External repositories and hosted starter projects linked by the retained bundler/framework guides use stock colours. They are labelled as upstream references. Individual documentation snippet exports and the 40 local examples are distinct and include the TQ theme. No hosted TQ npm package or externally published TQ starter is implied.

## Documentation deployment

The preview default is `http://127.0.0.1:5198`. Set `baseURL` in `docs-source/config.yml` to the HTTPS origin you own before rebuilding for publication. Check canonical links, the local assets and all three downloads at that destination. The build omits the upstream custom-domain CNAME; only add a CNAME for your own configured domain if your host requires it. Preview paths must not become the identity of a public deployment.
